source: https://open-design.ai/pricing — plan caps, credit multipliers and concurrency; token rates from the repo's own model catalogue where the id appears there (core/zen.json, else opencode-plugin/src/catalog.ts), otherwise estimated
creditUnit: 1 credit = $1 of the plan's allowance; a model spends list-price dollars x its multiplier
notes: Only the Go plan publishes a 5-hour cap; every plan publishes a monthly one.
The 7-day window resets from the subscription start, not Monday — the store records no subscription, so oduse cuts it as a rolling 7 days and says so.
plan-model credits are a second, published allowance with no local meter: the store names models, not which of them are plan models.
Every rate marked estimate is not published by Open Design; it is seeded from the closest published figure so a priced turn never reads as zero.

A model's id is the gateway's wire id — what `GET /v1/models` returns and what the store records on a turn — so a recorded id always keys a row. `catalogId` names the same model in core/zen.json where that catalogue spells it differently (a dot versus a dash); absent, the id is the same on both sides.
The multiplier for Claude Haiku 5.5 is 2x here while the billing page reads 4x; that conflict is open, so the value is left as published.
